nodes.label: laptop memory - visible progress is a hard requirement

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the laptop's live memory file - evidence of what this machine believed at that date, listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 7. The user must always be able to SEE that a process is alive and progressing. Failures that actually happened: a test script did one to three minutes of heavy imports before its first print, so he saw a dead terminal and killed it; runs were launched as agent background tasks invisible to him; and the harness progress bar only ticks when a whole question completes, so it sits frozen for minutes during queued model calls. He cannot distinguish queued-and-working from hung-and-dead without output, and he runs things himself in his own terminal, so the terminal experience IS the product. First print within about a second of launch - banner before heavy imports, each slow stage announced, flush=True; long waits need heartbeats ticking per model call rather than per finished question, with elapsed time moving; never run user-facing work as an agent background task; prefer streaming APIs where they exist, since a first token is proof of life. CANON_AUDIT.md 4.8 verdict: GROUNDED - he asked for it to be written into the .md
